records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts (execution 148.33) scored 0 of 8: four runs burned the entire 16384-token cap re-arguing the same two or three cases verbatim and never emitted a boxed answer, and the four that stopped all declared every branch contradictory yet still committed to one wrong survivor. The incumbent gives the elimination recipe but no budget, no loop-detection, and no rule for what to do when all branches look impossible, so the student spends its context restating settled cases instead of relaxing the extra assumption it imposed. This edit keeps the ordered information-set filtering, adds a legality check on implied values, forbids re-arguing settled cases, tells the student to relax its own added assumption when everything contradicts, and requires one final boxed answer - all failure modes that recur in any multi-round announcement puzzle, so it should transfer.

Fresh round-2 rollouts (execution_id 148.34) again scored 8/8, so the incumbent's substitution-plus-Mobius-image scaffold is exactly what works and must be preserved; the only leverage left is transfer. Six of eight traces spent effort on the false premise that the image is origin-centered (that |z| is constant), and the 13153-token outlier burned roughly double the median budget discovering and repairing that error mid-solution, while all eight landed on a quadratic whose x^2 and y^2 coefficients were not 1, the precise place a radius gets misread. This revision therefore leaves every word of the incumbent intact and only appends the non-origin warning plus an explicit normalize-then-complete-the-square step and a one-root check, unlike round 1's discarded rewrite which deleted the scaffold in favour of a generalized modulus shortcut and more than halved held-out accuracy.

Fresh round-2 rollouts scored 1/8: 7 of 8 hit the 16384-token cap and 5 of 8 emitted no boxed answer at all, yet 6 of 8 had already computed the exact overlap and correct total within the first 8-17 percent of the trace before abandoning it, so the bottleneck is still termination, not method. The dominant sink is a non-terminating search for a tangency or degenerate placement (20-70 tangency mentions and 28-53 'Alternatively' restarts per rollout); the single success was the one rollout that instead argued rotation cannot reduce the overlap and answered. The incumbent's abstract two-position invariance test was never actually executed (zero shoelace or invariance mentions), so this revision names the specific dead end to refuse, states the rotation-about-the-pinned-point argument that makes the overlap orientation-independent, and replaces 'commit at the end' with boxing the first exact value immediately.

Fresh round-2 rollouts (execution 148.36) scored 5/8, up from 0/8 at round 0, confirming the kept round-1 hint eliminated the cross-polynomial differencing dead end. All three remaining failures share one residual error: after correctly deriving the per-polynomial cap of deg P roots, and in one case even writing the menu-size-times-degree product, they collapse to the menu size because they treat each polynomial as supplying a single term rather than a whole block; the two that hit the 16384-token ceiling spent the tail looping over that same already-settled doubt. The revision keeps the working scaffold and adds the block-not-one-term correction, an explicit ban on answering the menu size, and a stop-re-deriving instruction to reclaim the truncated budget.

All eight rollouts were correct but every one burned thousands of tokens on two avoidable detours: inventing an unstated structural assumption (a named special shape / bisecting diagonals), hitting a contradiction, and then doubting the correct algebra instead of the assumption; and mis-pairing shoelace terms so the sum came out zero before a rescue via the cross product. The edit keeps the incumbent's concrete setup-then-area skeleton but replaces problem-specific machinery with two transferable rules - read only the stated constraint, and get area from a cross product at one vertex - so unseen constrained-points-on-a-curve problems avoid the same two dead ends.

records.mutation: reachability-first: free interleaving of pushes/pops, no premature impossible/certain, short-prefix decides bottom
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh round-2 rollouts scored 0/8, and the round-1 uniform-permutation error was largely suppressed: only one rollout still used 1/k, while the new dominant failure was a reachability error in the opposite direction, four rollouts asserting the buffer must be fully drained in truck order and so declared the target outcome outright impossible (probability 0) or the reverse order certain (probability 1), and two more looped to the length limit oscillating over the same claim. The revision therefore keeps the stack-shunting word framing and the bottom-equals-arrived-first rule but front-loads the missing fact that pushes and pops interleave freely with several items buffered, forbids declaring an outcome impossible or certain before exhibiting an admissible word, and states that the bottom event is settled by a short prefix so the student stops enumerating whole runs and terminates.

All 8 rollouts scored 0: six ran to the 16k generation cap without producing an answer, several built a wrong model of the setup (treating the unknown weights as polynomial coefficients) and then thrashed after deriving a contradiction or a free parameter, and the two that stopped guessed a value from an unconfirmed small-case pattern. Round 1 showed that adding more domain-specific interpolation machinery lowered held-out accuracy, so this edit removes the narrow vocabulary and instead installs a general procedure -- restate and count constraints, distrust a contradictory setup, hunt for one cancelling substitution rather than brute force, verify against the strongest given condition, and commit to one exact boxed value within budget -- which targets the thrash-and-overrun failure mode that should recur across unseen problems.

Fresh round-2 rollouts on the current incumbent scored 4/8, and all four failures shared one mechanism: the rollout read the stated subgroup count as the unknown item count, so it divided the totals by that number instead of by an admissible common divisor; two of them even skipped the gcd step entirely. The successes all did the same two extra things, which the incumbent only implied: they treated the stated subgroup count purely as a multiple-of filter on candidate counts, and when several divisors survived they resolved the ambiguity by taking the largest admissible one rather than guessing. This revision states both rules explicitly as reusable, noun-free checks while keeping the round-1 wins (gcd-of-totals divisibility, percent-base fixing, per-item integer back-check), which is the same generalization direction that raised held-out from 0.1125 to 0.1875.

The kept round-1 hint lifted fresh training from 0/8 to 4/8, and all four winners now terminate normally in 7.4k-10.8k tokens instead of every rollout hitting the 16384 cap, confirming that naming the involution ansatz concretely stopped the thrashing. The four residual failures split into three modes: one picked the reflection constant by guessing a midpoint of the two evaluation inputs rather than deriving it from the given constant terms, two abandoned the ansatz and reverted to multinomial coefficient matching of the composition, and one reached the correct values but then spent the rest of its cap re-verifying the composition with large numbers. This revision therefore gives the exact formula for the reflection constant, supplies the centered odd-power form that reduces the map to a single free parameter, and adds an explicit stopping rule once that parameter cancels.

In the fresh round-2 rollouts under the incumbent (2/8 correct) five of the six failures exhausted the completion cap: steered by the incumbent toward symbolic positional/bitwise algebra they mis-derived cycle structures, oscillated between rival closed forms, and never committed to an answer; the one finishing failure trusted an unverified decomposition and reported the period of a single sub-step. Budget exhaustion from abstract derivation now dominates, so this revision replaces that directive with one bounded concrete procedure - simulate literally on the smallest sizes, count repetitions to recurrence, fit and then confirm on an unused size - and treats measured counts as overruling any structural shortcut. Round 1 showed that stacking problem-specific cautions raised train but cut held-out, so this is phrased operation-agnostically and kept short.
